rationale: OC-ONT-8. An Objective-C method ATTRIBUTE is not part of the selector: `- (instancetype)initWithConfig:(NSDictionary *)config NS_DESIGNATED_INITIALIZER;` declares the selector `initWithConfig:`. The pinned grammar puts `NS_DESIGNATED_INITIALIZER` and `NS_REFINED_FOR_SWIFT` at the TOP LEVEL of the method node as a bare `identifier`, in two positions — after the last `method_parameter`, and after a zero-argument selector — and the selector rule appended it. Measured over the 322 admitted corpus files (2,891 method nodes): 79 nodes in 29 files, 30 distinct polluted selector names (`NS_REFINED_FOR_SWIFT` 62, `NS_DESIGNATED_INITIALIZER` 15, `NS_SWIFT_NOTHROW` 2). A polluted name loses the real symbol, so every message send to the real selector stops resolving to it and `overrides`' first-parent branch can never match it. The fix is POSITIONAL — a selector keyword always owns the `method_parameter` that follows it, so with parameters every leftover top-level identifier is an attribute and with none the first leftover is the zero-argument selector — which means no attribute name is hardcoded: an unknown macro cannot leak and a selector spelled like a macro cannot be dropped. The two attribute spellings the grammar gave their own node type (`NS_UNAVAILABLE` -> availability_attribute_specifier, `__attribute__((...))` -> attribute_specifier) were already safe and are pinned here so a rule change cannot break them.
